issue.title: QPIDJMS-315: Add support for Netty KQueue transport
issue.body:
Add KQueue support
Also add safer epoll and kqueue env check to protect from lib loading failure (as found in apache activemq artemis)

body: @michaelandrepearce are you packaging your own epoll artifact? There is currently no 32 bit support for epoll.

@johnou No we're not using artemis server is using netty-all and qpid clients are using individual deps , the isAvailable() check needs to take this into account though in its checks to detect if it is running in an environment its expected to be, before trying to load the native libs, e.g. really should only look to load native libs in an environment the libs are valid for, and if not isAvailable simply returns false. 

Ive sent in a PR

issue.title: ISSUE-7150 Add checks to load libs only in support environments.

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
To avoid attempts of native lib loading, only load the libs in environments currently  the native libs are build/provided for.

Motivation:

Netty should only attempt to load native libs, for environments that the native libs are provided, this avoids un-needed jvm warnings on isAvailable checks.

Modification:

Add checks for epoll, to only load in 64bit linux jvm
Add checks for kqueue, to only load in 64bit osx jvm

Result:

Fixes #https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/7150

If there is no issue then describe the changes introduced by this PR.

body: @michaelandrepearce but I am running a custom packaged epoll artifact which runs on 32 bit architecture so the suggested changes will break our application (in the sense that netty epoll will not be used).

@scottmitch 
It loads the lib but due to the bit complied on invocation (used by is available) it causes a native stack error and then the jvm has to unload i gracefully. It does continue, but this reliance that the jvm can catch this safely unload really should be avoided.

Re 32 bit custom builds, I think personally what is delivered in tested distributed build is what should be checked, if you have a custom build then you can custom update the check also.

Once/if netty provides a bundled/distributed 32 bit build then this would change but to deliver that a better native lib foldering and loading should be done like JNR project does with jffi.
Eg right now if a 32 bit and 64bit existed the netty all distro would overlay the two files as they would share the same fqn currrntly:

I would like to avoid getting into the "filtering what we support game" and instead rely upon the linker/architecture to detect these issues. Is there an option to modify the link/build commands to fail in a manner that is cleaner, or some other approach to improve detection?
As noted JNR uses a nice foldering structure and loading mechanism to support multiple bit builds and os specific builds. Maybe this could be adopted instead?

I note there is some override in the current hawtjni plugin that means it drops the platform folder (that would already separate by os and arch), any specific reason? I ask as this is similar way that JNR does this, and if used along with using the hawtjni Library.load which has logic to look in the correct folder for the right platform (os+arch) would help this issue.
One could also argue it's a deployment issue (incorrect jar on the classpath), the classifier for the jar is  linux-x86_64..

As noted dependency is on netty all (contains epoll and kqueue), and surely this is the point of the isAvailable check so code can see if it can safely use and then if not failback, aka back onto nio.
Back to resolving this, is there any particular reason why overriding the default hawtjni and not use its loader?

issue.title: Only load native transport if running architecture match the compiled…

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
… library architecture.

Motivation:

We should only try to load the native artifacts if the architecture we are currently running on is the same as the one the native libraries were compiled for.

Modifications:

Include architecture in native lib name and append the current arch when trying to load these. This will fail then if its not the same as the arch of the compiled arch.

Result:

Fixes [#7150].
